CS3-H-03.note: The refutation contrasts scribal hands with compass-built capitals copying carved inscriptions, i.e. vernacular vs classical; 'vernacular' names the same discarded claim (letters his hand already knew) and survives the whole passage.

CS3-H-07.note: 'Discretionary' is defensible: seniors 'save it for the years in which nothing else will do', which is exercise at the holder's judgment. I take 'latent' because the sentence's point is that the power is present but unmanifest ('not weak; simply expensive'), and discretion is already given by 'may call' in sentence 1.

CS3-H-15.note: B is the only option that is both fully staged and hedged ('a conclusion neither result alone would support'); the other three each assert something a structure option rarely gets to say (predicts a design, endorses the older answer, meaning unknown). Pickable on option shape alone.

CS3-H-16.note: C is defensible: sentence 1 states the two are one body, so treating them as separate was an error, and 'not simple ignorance' plus the 1960s models makes it understandable. I prefer A because the sentence's thrust is a justification (a rule nobody can administer is not a rule), not a concession, but a scorer would have to work to reject C.

CS3-H-18.note: C is the only constructive option; A, B and D are each a denial or a doubt of something a responding author would normally have to grant. The option set alone points at C.
